items.title: Accelerator cable can stick
items.summary: The accelerator cable can stick, so engine speed doesn't drop immediately when you lift off the pedal.

items.title: Camshaft seal end plug can dislodge
items.summary: Expansion and contraction of the cylinder head can push out the camshaft seal end plug and let oil leak from the camshaft.

items.title: Rear center seat-belt buckle
items.summary: Some trucks were built with a rear center buckle meant for another market.

items.title: Front hub missing lock washer or screws
items.summary: Some trucks were built without a lock washer and/or screws in the front hub.

items.title: Left front brake line clearance
items.summary: The left front brake lines were installed with too little clearance to the upper control arm.

items.title: Transfer case flange nuts
items.summary: Transfer-case flange nuts weren't installed properly and could loosen.

items.title: TOD trucks: fuel leak in a frontal crash
items.summary: On 4WD automatic trucks with Torque On Demand, a high-speed frontal crash could separate an interior fuel line and hose or move engine-bay parts, risking a fuel leak.

tsbs.title: Intake manifold gaskets (1998)
tsbs.summary: Owners writing to NHTSA mention a 1998 service bulletin for faulty intake gaskets, and Edmunds owners call the 3.5's intake gasket a common warranty repair. Bulletin number not confirmed.

timeline.change: December: all-new Trooper (Bighorn) launched as a 1992 model; 3.2 L V6 in SOHC (175 hp) and DOHC (190 hp) forms, auto hubs, four-wheel discs
Bighorn receives the 1992/93 Japan Car of the Year Special Award
Three-door RS sold in the US
Revised 190 hp SOHC 3.2; shift-on-the-fly on some trucks; Acura SLX twin launched (November 1995)
Consumer Reports rates the 1995–96 Trooper and SLX 'Not Acceptable' (August 1996); NHTSA denies a defect petition (July 1997)
Facelift, 3.5 L 6VE1 (215 hp / 230 lb-ft) and Borg-Warner Torque On Demand on some trims

Peak years for NHTSA complaints about 3.5 oil consumption, engines running dry and stalling: by our keyword count, about 38 of the 81 complaints for 1999 describe heavy oil use or seizure. CarComplaints rates 2000 as the worst Trooper year, mainly for transmission failures. Check any 3.5 carefully
Last Acura SLX (6,590 sold in the US in total)
New grille; Grade Logic downshift control on automatics (2000–02)
Last US model year; the final Japanese Bighorn is built in September 2002

identify.intro: The UBS was sold under at least nine badges, and the US got only the V6s, so it pays to know which truck and which drivetrain you're looking at.

items.head: Chassis codes
items.body: UBS25 = 3.2 L 6VD1 V6, UBS26 = 3.5 L 6VE1 V6, UBS69 = 3.1 L 4JG2 turbo-diesel, UBS73 = 3.0 L 4JX1 turbo-diesel. Japanese model codes add a prefix and suffix, for example E-UBS25GW or KD-UBS69GW.

items.head: 3.2 or 3.5
items.body: 1992–97 US trucks have the 3.2 (SOHC on the S, DOHC on the 1992–95 LS); 1998–2002 trucks have the 3.5 DOHC. The 1998 facelift, with new lamps and fenders and a body-colored hard spare cover, is the easy visual tell.

items.head: Torque On Demand
items.body: TOD trucks (1998 on, S Performance and S Luxury at first) have a '4WD Auto' mode and a TOD indicator. Part-time trucks don't.

items.head: Acura SLX
items.body: Sold for the 1996–99 model years, automatic only, with the 3.2 and then (from 1998) the 3.5 and TOD. Mechanically a Trooper with Acura trim.

items.head: Re-badges and imports
items.body: Holden Jackaroo and Monterey, Opel and Vauxhall Monterey, Honda Horizon, Subaru Bighorn, Chevrolet Trooper and HSV Jackaroo are all UBS. Diesels and right-hand drive mean an import.

paragraphs: The UBS diesels (the 3.1-liter 4JG2 and, from 1998, the 3.0-liter 4JX1) were never sold in the US, nor were the Holden, Opel, Vauxhall, Honda and Subaru versions. Trucks built at least 25 years ago can be imported under the US 25-year exemption, so in 2026 that covers UBS production from 2001 and earlier, one build month at a time.
Check your state's titling and emissions rules before buying an imported diesel. California is the most difficult.
